scheme_name: "Immediate Death Relief Assistance" under "Welfare and Relief for Fishermen During Lean Seasons and Natural Calamities Scheme"
description:
The "Immediate Death Relief Assistance" is a crucial component of the "Welfare and Relief for Fishermen During Lean Seasons and Natural Calamities Scheme" launched by the Government of India.

This scheme was officially launched on 1st April 2018.

It was initiated to provide timely financial assistance to the families of fishermen who face the unfortunate event of death due to various reasons.

The primary objective of the Immediate Death Relief Assistance is to ensure that the families of deceased fishermen do not face financial hardships during their time of grief.

The scheme aims to provide immediate financial support to the families to help them cope with the loss of their primary breadwinner.

Under this scheme, the government provides a one-time financial assistance of ₹2 lakh to the family of the deceased fisherman.

This amount is intended to cover immediate expenses and provide some financial stability to the family during a difficult time.

The assistance is provided irrespective of the cause of death, which includes accidents at sea, natural calamities, or any other unforeseen circumstances.

The eligibility criteria for receiving the Immediate Death Relief Assistance are specific and straightforward.

The applicant must be a registered fisherman under the relevant state fisheries department.

The fisherman must have been actively engaged in fishing activities at the time of death.

The family of the deceased fisherman must provide proof of their relationship to the deceased.

The age of the deceased fisherman must be at least 18 years at the time of death.

The application process for the Immediate Death Relief Assistance is designed to be user-friendly.

The family members of the deceased fisherman must approach the local fisheries department office to initiate the application process.

They are required to fill out an application form that can be obtained from the fisheries department.

The application form must be accompanied by specific documents including the death certificate of the fisherman.

The family must also provide proof of registration of the deceased fisherman with the fisheries department.

Additionally, identity proof of the applicant must be submitted, which can include Aadhar card, voter ID, or any government-issued ID.

Once the application is submitted, the fisheries department will verify the documents and the eligibility of the applicant.

The verification process is typically completed within 15 days from the date of application submission.

Upon successful verification, the financial assistance of ₹2 lakh is disbursed to the family of the deceased fisherman.

The disbursement is made through direct bank transfer to the bank account of the applicant.

This ensures that the funds are transferred securely and promptly to the family in need.

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying at the central level.

At the state level, the respective fisheries departments are responsible for the execution and monitoring of the scheme.

Each state has designated officials who oversee the implementation of the scheme and assist families in the application process.

The scheme is particularly significant for coastal states where fishing is a primary source of livelihood for many families.

The government has allocated substantial funds to ensure the effective implementation of this scheme.

In the financial year 2021-2022, the government allocated ₹200 crore for the welfare and relief schemes for fishermen.

This allocation reflects the government's commitment to supporting the fishing community during challenging times.

The scheme also aims to create awareness among fishermen about their rights and the available assistance.

Workshops and information sessions are conducted by the fisheries department to educate fishermen about the scheme.

The Immediate Death Relief Assistance is part of a broader initiative to provide social security to fishermen.

The government recognizes the vulnerabilities faced by fishermen due to the nature of their work.

Natural calamities such as cyclones and floods can severely impact their livelihoods and safety.

The scheme is designed to act as a safety net for families during such crises.

Statistical data indicates that a significant percentage of fishermen face risks associated with their profession.

According to the National Fisheries Development Board, approximately 14 million people are engaged in fishing activities in India.

The fishing community often lacks adequate financial security and insurance coverage.

This makes schemes like the Immediate Death Relief Assistance vital for their welfare.

The government continuously monitors the impact of the scheme and makes necessary adjustments based on feedback from beneficiaries.

The scheme has received positive responses from various stakeholders in the fishing community.

Many families have expressed gratitude for the timely assistance provided under this scheme.

The government encourages families to utilize the assistance for essential needs such as education, healthcare, and daily expenses.

The Immediate Death Relief Assistance is a testament to the government's commitment to supporting vulnerable communities.

It reflects a proactive approach to addressing the challenges faced by fishermen and their families.

The scheme also aligns with the broader goals of the government to enhance the socio-economic conditions of marginalized groups.

The government aims to ensure that no family is left in distress due to the loss of a breadwinner.

Overall, the Immediate Death Relief Assistance is a significant welfare initiative that provides crucial support to the families of fishermen in India.

It serves as a lifeline during times of grief and financial uncertainty.

The scheme exemplifies the government's dedication to the welfare of the fishing community and their resilience in the face of adversity.
